theme: 3 SwiftUI terms for keyboards, menus and pointers on iPad and Mac

terms.definition: A modifier that lets people trigger a button with keys on a keyboard.
terms.example: Add keyboardShortcut to the Save button.

terms.definition: A menu in the menu bar that holds your own commands.
terms.example: Put the export actions in a CommandMenu.

terms.definition: A modifier that makes a view react when a pointer moves over it.
terms.example: Add hoverEffect so the button lifts under the pointer.

video.description:
Learn to explain how to support keyboards, menus and pointers in SwiftUI apps: keyboardShortcut, CommandMenu & hoverEffect, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
keyboardShortcut - A modifier that lets people trigger a button with keys on a keyboard.
CommandMenu - A menu in the menu bar that holds your own commands.
hoverEffect - A modifier that makes a view react when a pointer moves over it.

Quiz at the end - write your answers in the comments, then watch again to check.

landscape.hook: Can you explain keyboardShortcut, CommandMenu and hoverEffect in English?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, my iPad app needs to work well with a keyboard.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Add keyboardShortcut to the Save button, with the letter `s`.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So users press command and S to save?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes, keyboardShortcut adds the command key for you by default.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Where can users see shortcuts on a Mac or an iPad?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: In the menu bar. Add a CommandMenu for your own tools.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Buttons, like Run. The CommandMenu shows them in a new menu with your title.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Last, I use a trackpad. The buttons do not react when I point at them.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Add hoverEffect. With `.lift`, the button grows a little under the pointer.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Does hoverEffect work on touch screens?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Not on touch alone. It needs a pointer.
